hook.text: The joule is the standard unit of energy—named after James Joule, who linked heat and mechanical work.

buildup.text: One joule is the energy needed to lift a small apple one meter—roughly equivalent to one newton-meter of work.

discovery.text: A running human produces about 75 joules per second (75 watts)—a lightbulb and a person use similar power.

twist.text: A single candy bar contains about 1 million joules—enough energy to power a 100-watt bulb for nearly 3 hours.

climax.text: Global energy consumption is about 580 exajoules per year—that's 580 followed by 18 zeros.

punchline.text: From an apple lift to global grids—joules measure it all.

quiz.question: How much energy does a candy bar contain?
